what: Sailor's rulings on lines — the closed form's labelled examples. Every run shows them to the model as ruled cases; each entry is one line he has scored or corrected, with his reason. Add by telling Claude (or by hand). The relational test: Parameters/02_Protocols/Diatribe_Derivation_Protocol_Revision.md, Step 3 codified (2026-11-05).

principles.name: reported speech
principles.rule: When a speaker passes on someone else's view, it depends on how he presents it. If he affirms its logic, score it as his own. If he presents it as a specimen (a barometer, an example of what others believe), score his framing of it, not the view.
principles.case: captive dreamer 2026-11-04: his 2024 Trump friend's year of Epstein and 'Israel controlling Trump', offered as 'a good barometer'

principles.name: the self-settled wager
principles.rule: When a speaker sets a test of his own (a bet, 'wake me up when that changes') and then pays it out himself before it can be applied ('even if there were, I don't care anymore'), the line is closed: 'even if' answers every reply in advance. Settling your own test is capital spent. The object is sacrificed to keep the reaction; the line leaves z (shadow). Pattern #29.
principles.case: captive dreamer 2026-02-28, the bet settled early (crystal line 20)

principles.name: restated record
principles.rule: A speaker's claim about his own past ('I always said', 'I was skeptical from the start') is a dated-record claim: check it against the set. If the earlier lines bear it out, it is an open statement (fluid). If they contradict it, it is an argument built to reposition him in front of the audience (working, coalition) and carries #8, the past revised to fit the present. The set decides the tier, not the words.
principles.case: captive dreamer 2026-03-06 and 2026-08-28 (crystal lines 21, 25) against his June–July 2025 lines

principles.name: as said on the day
principles.rule: A line is placed in the band it had on the day it was said. If later events make it look closed, it stays where it was: the turn is carried by the forecast scoring, which reads the line again when it comes due. Hindsight never re-reads a line.
principles.case: captive dreamer 2025-06-13 'Wake me up when that changes' and 2025-06-22 'that WONT happen': working the room on the day, closed only in retrospect

principles.name: a hypothetical is not a forecast
principles.rule: A judgment about something if it happened ('X would be a mistake', 'we should never do X') says what the speaker thinks of X, not that X will or won't happen. It is a statement of position: no due date, no forecast scoring.
principles.case: captive dreamer 2026-02-28 'I think boots on ground would be a big mistake and still do!' — read by the forecast pass as a forecast of boots; ruled not a forecast

principles.name: z is read against the Object
principles.rule: z says whether the Object of political economy is realized (+1) or frustrated (-1). It is read against the Object itself, never against what an audience wants. What the Object is realizing is left open.
principles.case: the dollar: a falling share is frustrated, and what it frustrates is the Object

principles.name: a pattern is not a prediction
principles.rule: A line Prism states about the Object's own behaviour (P3) is a possible pattern. It has no due date and is never scored right or wrong. It is read against its measure on a rolling basis, and each reading says whether the pattern holds.
principles.case: P3, the hemisphere barrel: read against the dollar every month from 2026-12-31. 'We aren't trying to check the prediction, we are just tracking the market in terms of political economy.'

principles.name: one chamber passing
principles.rule: On the law: both chambers passing the same resolution reads +0.5; one chamber passing reads +0.35; a recorded vote held reads +0.2; a vote kept from the floor reads -0.5.
principles.case: House leadership pulled the vote on 2026-05-21 (-0.5); the House passed H.Con.Res. 86 on 06-03 (+0.35); the Senate agreed to it on 06-23 (+0.5)

principles.name: a fact held up as a complaint
principles.rule: A line that states a bad state has come, as a fact, reads leaning frustrated. It is the mirror of the line that says a bad state has not come (leaning realized). Judged by the words.
principles.case: Tucker 2026-10-23: 'We're spending more a year on the military in adjusted dollars than we did during World War II.' Sailor: he is dissatisfied with money spent toward belligerent ends he disagrees with.

principles.name: the band of a prayer
principles.rule: Being a prayer does not set the band. What the prayer says about other people does. A prayer that tells the room to shut a side out, or calls the other side's position a spell, is a verdict (closed, denominated). A prayer that names no one stays open (fluid). Its z is still neither: a prayer looks forward.
principles.case: Tucker 2025-06-05 'Pray that Donald Trump ignores them.' and 2026-03-09 'Pray that the spell breaks and the world is saved.' read denominated; 2026-03-02, the Prince of Peace prayer, reads fluid (Sailor 11-16).

principles.name: the speaker on himself
principles.rule: A line about what kind of person someone is, is shadow, and that holds when the person is the speaker. A line about his own record or his own attitude is about him, not the object. A line stating his position on the object itself stays object. The band of a record claim is still decided by the set (see 'restated record').
principles.case: captive dreamer 2026-11-05 'I explicitly opposed the Iran war from the outset' and 2026-03-06 'I'm willing to give Trump the benefit of the doubt.' are shadow; 'I'm skeptical of these strikes' stays object (Sailor 11-16).

principles.name: a question is a question
principles.rule: A question is read as a question unless the post answers it itself. Do not read a charge or a motive into it. Judged by the words: a question the other side can answer pronounces nothing on anyone, so it is open (fluid). If the speaker states the thing instead of asking it, that is a verdict.
principles.case: Tucker 2026-03-05 'Could this be a religious war designed to rebuild the Third Temple on the ashes of Al Aqsa? Hope not.' is about the object, leaning frustrated, fluid. Sailor 11-16: a statement of perception, he is expressing his shock at these patterns.

principles.name: a teaser is the whole post
principles.rule: When a post ends by handing its questions to a guest or an episode ('X has the numbers'), every line in it is a teaser, including a factual line at the top. Teaser lines are kept apart and labelled.
principles.case: Tucker 2026-10-23: 'We're spending more a year on the military... What are we getting for it? And how much is going to Israel? Stephen Semler has the numbers.' No reader marked it a teaser on 11-16.

rhetorical: a hope looks forward without saying what will happen (Sailor 11-16)
